Denise Rosado

Republican candidate for Delegate to the House of Representatives from the District of Columbia · Open seat

Attorney (immigration attorney; principal of Denise Rosado PLLC)

Denise Rosado is an attorney in Washington, D.C., and the Republican nominee for D.C.'s non-voting Delegate to the U.S. House. She describes herself as a former Democrat who is now a Republican. She won the June 16, 2026 Republican primary and is running in the November 3 general election for the seat Eleanor Holmes Norton is leaving.

Where Rosado stands

Public safety / federal law enforcement
Supports D.C. working with federal law enforcement when needed, and says data shows crime went down while federal law enforcement was present. Calls for tougher sentencing and what she calls real prosecution.
Federal taxes / representation
Says that because D.C. residents have no vote in Congress, they should not pay federal income tax, as is the case in Puerto Rico, Guam and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
Housing
Proposes turning empty buildings into housing and pushing for new development quickly, arguing that more housing supply will make housing more affordable.
Economy / downtown jobs
Says businesses were driven out of downtown and pledges to seek federal incentives to bring jobs back. Proposes making D.C. a national hub for AI and cybersecurity.
Education
Argues that D.C. spends more per student than almost any other U.S. city but gets worse results, and blames city leadership.
